title: The price is right
prompt:
The starter reads a price in cents and a quantity straight into two words in `.data`, `price` and `quantity`. Multiply them and store the product in the third word, `total`. The last lines of the starter load all three words back out of memory and print them, so the bill only shows up if it really is in `total`.

A value in `.data` takes two loads to reach: `ldr x9, =price` puts the address of `price` in `x9`, then `ldr w10, [x9]` fetches the 32-bit value stored at that address. `str` goes the other way: `str w12, [x9]` writes `w12` to the address in `x9`.

## what is checked

- with input `1299 3` the line reads `3 x 1299 cents = 3897 cents`
- the program exits cleanly
- `mul` works out the bill and `str` writes it to memory
- the program also runs on prices and quantities you do not see, including a quantity of 0 and a negative quantity (items handed back)
starter:
// work out a bill from a price and a quantity kept in .data
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

.data
        .balign 4
price:      .word 0                         // cents for one item, read from input
quantity:   .word 0                         // how many, read from input
total:      .word 0                         // price times quantity belongs here
fmt_in:     .string "%d %d"
fmt_out:    .string "%d x %d cents = %d cents\n"

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // scanf writes straight into both words
        ldr     x1, =price
        ldr     x2, =quantity
        bl      scanf

        // TODO: load price and quantity from memory, multiply them,
        // and store the product in total

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out                // print all three words from memory
        ldr     x9, =quantity
        ldr     w1, [x9]
        ldr     x9, =price
        ldr     w2, [x9]
        ldr     x9, =total
        ldr     w3, [x9]
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
